title: Valle d'Aosta's Pumps Run Above the National Average as August Draws to a Close
dek: Italy's smallest region pays a small but consistent premium on self-service Benzina and Gasolio, even as its 85-station network holds steady.
body: Drivers in Valle d'Aosta paid €2.043 per litre for self-service Benzina and €2.183 for Gasolio as of August 29 — both above the national self-service averages of €2.029 and €2.160. The gap is modest, about 1.3 cents on petrol and 2.2 cents on diesel, roughly 0.7% and 1.0% respectively, but it has held through the whole of August: this small, mountainous region rarely undercuts the rest of the country at the pump.

The trend over the past ten tracked days has been upward. Self-service Benzina climbed from €2.029 on August 20 to a local peak of €2.045 on August 27, before easing back slightly to €2.043 by month's end. Gasolio traced the same arc, rising from €2.164 to a peak of €2.184 before settling at €2.183. Through all of it the region's station network stayed remarkably steady: 85 registered outlets with 70 reporting prices on the latest day, an 82% reporting rate that hasn't moved all month.

Tracking that kind of daily push-and-pull, for all twenty of Italy's regions at once, cross-checked against the national picture every morning, is exactly the sort of thing a hand-updated spreadsheet quietly stops doing after a few weeks. Fuel Dashboard pulls straight from Italy's MIMIT open data feed and rebuilds itself automatically each day — no manual copy-paste, no stale numbers — a pipeline built with Claude Code that turns what used to be a recurring chore into something that just runs.
pull_quote: Valle d'Aosta's diesel now costs over 2 cents more per litre than the Italian average — and it's still climbing.
caption:
Today's regional spotlight on Fuel Dashboard: Valle d'Aosta, where self-service Gasolio is running about 2.2 cents above Italy's national average at €2.183/L, and Benzina sits roughly 1.3 cents over the national mean at €2.043/L. Both have been drifting upward through most of August.

Fuel Dashboard tracks fuel prices across all 23,973 registered stations in Italy, updates itself every day straight from the MIMIT open data feed, and rotates through a different region each day for a closer look — no manual spreadsheet, no stale numbers. Check today's numbers and the rest of the country at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

This is also a small case study in what's now possible with AI coding tools: the entire pipeline, from data ingestion to the daily regional write-up you're reading, was built and is maintained with Claude Code. A few years ago this would have been a manually maintained Excel sheet updated (or forgotten) once a week. Now it's a live dashboard that refreshes itself every morning without anyone touching it.
